calls.head: The Red Wings like DeBrincat’s line against Wennberg’s
calls.body: At home, the Red Wings keep sending DeBrincat’s line (Brandsegg-Nygård, Finnie and DeBrincat) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Todd McLellan keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Sharks’ second line is Marchment, Wennberg and Toffoli.
calls.call: The Red Wings’ L2 (Brandsegg-Nygård, Finnie and DeBrincat) spends at least 36% of its 5-on-5 time against the Sharks’ second line, against about 26% with no line matching.

calls.head: Penalties could cost the Sharks
calls.body: The Red Wings’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Sharks’ kill is one of the worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Sharks more than most.

DET.head: We gave Detroit a 62% chance, and they delivered.

SJS.head: We gave San Jose only a 38% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Finnie sparks a Red Wings comeback
paras: Justin Faulk got the scoring started for the Red Wings on the power play midway through the first. Late in the first, Keegan Kolesar and Barclay Goodrow fought, and Dmitry Orlov tied it up for San Jose on the power play. Macklin Celebrini put the Sharks ahead 2-1 early in the second. Ivar Stenberg made it 3-1 on the power play early in the third, but Emmitt Finnie pulled the Wings within one a little over two minutes later. With the goalie pulled and a minute and a half left, Alex DeBrincat tied it 3-3. Lucas Raymond scored the only goal of the shootout for the Red Wings. Celebrini finished with a goal and two assists.

The Sharks had a little more of the play and hit a post and the crossbar, but the Red Wings had the finish. John Gibson, who gave up five goals against New Jersey in his last start, made 31 saves for the Red Wings, and Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 24 of 27 at the other end. The Red Wings moved to 3-3-2 and climbed off the bottom of the Atlantic to seventh, while the Sharks fell to 4-3-1 but climbed to fourth in the Pacific.

items.text: Dmitry Orlov scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 21 (21 games played since).
Alex DeBrincat is now one goal from 300.
